args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 (and its staging candidate v2.3.1-rc) were marked unhealthy. Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback status: healthy in all regions on v2.3.0, error rate 0.2%. Follow-up: investigate the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying. Also note v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging but was still promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001), which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0, health checks pass and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the current status. It also says to find the cause of the v2.3.1 failure before deploying it again.

v2.3.1's release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also marked unhealthy in staging, but it was still released to production. I noted this in the incident so the team can look at why it wasn't stopped.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
